title: Flattening a large array JSON in PySpark and converting to dataframe
question:
I've a couple of tables that are sent from source system in array Json format, like in the below example. Each table could have different number of rows. For instance, the Table1 could have 1m rows, and Table2 could have 10m.

schema = StructType([
StructField("Table1", StructType([
    StructField("Col1", ArrayType(IntegerType()), True),
    StructField("Col2", ArrayType(LongType()), True)
]), True),
StructField("Table2", StructType([
    StructField("Col1", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
    StructField("Col2", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
    StructField("Col3", ArrayType(LongType()), True)
]), True))]

The size of the Json input file is about 8GB. I need to get the Json array columns into spark dataframe and write to Lakehouse as Table1 and Table2.

I know the schema before the transformation, but whenever I try to flatten using explode, I get the error that the row size is greater than 2GB. Exact error below:

Is there a way I can explode the data into array while reading the JSON file?
answer:
2GB limit exceed could be due to a single column exceeding or the whole row exceeding after the explode.

Check if you have any columns that could exceed the 2GB limit after deserialization when you do explode. If so you might have to see how to handle that column if it is really needed. May be compress it. Couple of articles below on how you could go about it.
https://community.databricks.com/t5/data-engineering/how-to-efficiently-process-a-50gb-json-file-and-store-it-in/td-p/23756
How to overcome the 2GB limit for a single column value in Spark

If it is the single record/row that exceeds limit perhaps you can chunk it into multiple files or add some filter while reading like timestamp etc to process it in multiple steps.
